'''Stuart J. Rowan''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 1969) is a Scottish chemist.

== Early life and education ==
Rowan was born in [[Edinburgh]] on October 16, 1969, and raised in [[Troon]], [[South Ayrshire]]. He completed a Bachelor of Science in chemistry at the [[University of Glasgow]].

Rowan earned his doctorate from the Chemistry Department at the [[University of Glasgow]] under the direction of David D. MacNicol in 1994 working on Supramolecular Crystal Engineering. ([https://theses.gla.ac.uk/75368/ Thesis])

In late 1994, he began postdoctoral working for [[Jeremy Sanders]] in the Chemistry Department at the [[University of Cambridge]] working on dynamic covalent libraries.<ref>(refs: Rowan, S.J.; Hamilton, D.G.; Brady, P.A.; Sanders, J.K.M. Automated Recognition, Sorting and Covalent Self-Assembly by Predisposed Building Blocks in a Mixture J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1997, 119, 2578–2579. Rowan, S.J.; Sanders, J.K.M. Building Thermodynamic Combinatorial Libraries of Quinine Macrocylces Chem. Commun. 1997, 1407–1408.)</ref>

== Career ==
In 1998, Rowan left the United Kingdom to continue his postdoctoral studies with Nobel Laureate [[Fraser Stoddart|Sir J. Fraser Stoddart]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sir J. Fraser Stoddart – Biographical |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2016/stoddart/biographical/%202016/ |access-date=2025-09-28 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> where he worked on using dynamic covalent chemistry in the synthesis of interlocked  molecules.<ref>(ref Rowan, S.J.; Stoddart, J.F. Thermodynamic Template-Directed Synthesis of Dynamic Rotaxanes by Imine Exchange Org. Lett. 1999, 1, 1913-1916.)</ref> He also developed Surrogate phosphonium stoppers for rotaxanes that could be exchanged using Wittig chemistry.<ref>(ref Rowan, S.J.; Stoddart, J.F. Precision Molecular Grafting: Exchanging Surrogate Stoppers in [2]Rotaxanes J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2000, 122, 164-165.)</ref>

In 1999, he was appointed as an assistant professor in the Department of Macromolecular Science and Engineering at [[Case Western Reserve University]] in Cleveland, Ohio. In 2005, he was promoted to Associate Professor with tenure and became a Full Professor in 2008. In 2009, he was named the Kent Hale Smith Professor of Engineering.<ref name="cwru">{{cite news |author = Rowan, Stuart & CWRU Staff | date = 11 October 2021 | title=Dr. Stuart Rowan |url=https://engineering.case.edu/groups/supramolecular/StuartRowan |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011112819/https://engineering.case.edu/groups/supramolecular/StuartRowan |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 11, 2021 |access-date=11 October 2021 |publisher=Case Western Reserve University}}</ref> There he starting working supramolecular materials using nucleobases <ref>(Sivakova, S.; Bohnsack, D.A.; Suwanmala, P.; Mackay, M.E.; Rowan, S.J. Utilization of a Combination of Weak Hydrogen Bonding Interactions and Phase Segregation to Yield Highly Thermo-Sensitive Supramolecular Polymers J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 18202-18211. Buerkle, L.E.; von Recum, H.A.; Rowan S.J. Toward Potential New Supramolecular Tissue Engineering Scaffolds Based on Guanosine Derivatives Chem. Sci. 2012, 3, 564-572.)</ref> and pi-pi interactions,<ref>(with Howard Colquhoun and Wayne Hayes) (ref: Burattini, S.; Greenland, B.W.; Merino D.H., Weng, W.; Seppala, J.; Colquhoun, H.M.; Hayes, W.; Mackay, M.E.; Hamley, I.W.; Rowan S.J. A healable supramolecular polymer blend based on aromatic π-π stacking and hydrogen bonding interactions J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2010, 132, 12051-12058)</ref> metallosupramolecular polymers <ref>(Beck, J.B.; Rowan, S.J. Multi-Stimuli, Multi-Responsive Metallo-Supramolecular Polymers, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2003, 125, 13922-13923.; Burnworth, M.; Tang, L.; Kumpfer, J.R., Duncan, A. J., Beyer, F.L.; Fiore, G.L.; Rowan S.J.; Weder, C. Optically Healable Supramolecular Polymers Nature 2011, 472, 334-337. DOI: 10.1038/nature09963.),</ref> and mechanically adaptive cellulose nanocrystal composites (with Christoph Weder).<ref>(ref: Capadona, J.R.; Shanmuganathan, K.; Tyler D.J.; Rowan S.J.; Weder, C. Stimuli-Responsive Polymer Nanocomposites Inspired by the Sea Cucumber Dermis Science 2008, 319, 1370-1374. DOI: 10.1126/science.1153307.)</ref> During his time at CWRU he was awarded the NSF CAREER Award, the Morley Medal from the Cleveland Section of the American Chemical Society in 2014 <ref>(https://www.acscleveland.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Morley_winners_2025.pdf)</ref> and the Herman Mark Scholar Award from the American Chemical Society in 2015.<ref>(https://polyacs.org/marks-scholar-awards/)</ref>

In 2016, Rowan joined [[The University of Chicago]]'s [[Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering]] as well as that university's Department of Chemistry,<ref name="pme">{{cite news |author = Rowan, Stuart & PME Staff | date = 11 October 2021 | title=Stuart Rowan |url=https://pme.uchicago.edu/faculty/stuart-rowan |access-date=11 October 2021 |publisher=Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering}}</ref> and accepted an appointment as the Barry L. MacLean Professor for Molecular Engineering Innovation and Enterprise in 2018.<ref name="ucchem">{{cite news |author = Rowan, Stuart & PSD Staff | date = 11 October 2021 | title=Stuart Rowan |url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/stuart-rowan |access-date=11 October 2021 |publisher=Physical Sciences Division, The University of Chicago}}</ref> Rowan also holds a staff scientist position at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name="pme" />

In June 2026, Rowan also was named Director of the Energy Technologies initiative, a partnership between the Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth and the UChicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (UChicago PME)<ref>https://pme.uchicago.edu/news-events/news/energy-technologies-initiative-receive-new-leadership</ref>.

At the University of Chicago, his research group have continued to carry out the exploration of dynamic covalent networks using primarily disulfide bonds and  room temperature dynamic, catalyst free thia-Michael bonds. His group has pioneered the use of dynamic covalent networks to access pluripotent plastics.<ref>(Boynton, N.R.; Dennis, J.M.; Dolinski, N.D.; Lindberg, C.A.; Kotula, A.P.; Grocke, G.L.; Vivod, S.L.; Lenhart, J.L.; Patel, S.N.; Rowan, S.J. Toward pluripotent materials through tempering of dynamic covalent polymer networks Science 2024, 383, 545-551. DOI: 10.1126/science.adi5009)</ref> With Henrich Jaegar his group has developed dynamic covalent dense suspensions that exhibit time dependent rheopectic behavior.<ref>(Kim, H.; Livermore, S.M.; Rowan, S.J.; Jaeger, H.M. Dense suspensions as trainable rheological metafluids Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 2025 122, e2509525122. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2509525122; Kim, H.; van der Naald, M.; Dolinski, N.D.; Rowan, S.J.; Jaegar, H.M. Dynamic-bond-induced Sticky Friction Tailors Non-Newtonian Rheology Soft Matter 2023, 19, 6797-6804. DOI: 10.1039/D3SM00479A)</ref>

His group have also developed the first synthetic route to poly[n]catenanes <ref>(Wu, Q.; Lang, X.; Rauscher, P.M.; Wojtecki, R.J.; de Pablo, J.J.; Hore, M.J.A.; Rowan, S.J. Poly[n]catenanes: Synthesis of molecular interlocked chains Science, 2017, 358, 1434-1439. DOI: 10.1126/science.aap7675.)</ref> and slide ring polycatenanes <ref>(Hart, L.F.; Lenart, W.R.; Hertzog, J.E.; Oh, J.; Turner, W.R.; Dennis, J.M.; Rowan, S.J. Doubly-Threaded Slide-Ring Polycatenane Networks J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2023, 145, 12315–12323. DOI: 10.1021/jacs.3c02837)</ref> prepared biographene from biowaste <ref>(Hui, J.; You, H.; Van Beek, A.; Zhang, J.; Elahi, A.; Downing, J.R.; Chaney, L.E.; Lee, D.; Ainsworth, E.A. Chaudhuri, S.; Dunn, J.B.; Chen, W.; Rowan, S.J.; Hersam, M.C. Sustainable Production of Biomass-Derived Graphite and Graphene Conductive Inks from Biochar Small, 2024, 2406669. DOI 10.1002/smll.202406669.),</ref> has programs working on all organic batteries <ref>(Grocke, G.L.; Zhang, H.; Kopfinger, S.S.; Patel, S.N.; Rowan, S.J. Synthesis and characterization of redox-responsive disulfide-crosslinked polymer particles for energy storage applications, ACS Macro Lett. 2021, 10, 1637–1642. DOI: 10.1021/acsmacrolett.1c00682;  Alessandri, R.; Li, C.-H.; Keating, S.; Mohanty, K.T.; Peng, A.; Lutkenhaus, J.L.; Rowan, S.J.; Tabor, D.P.; de Pablo, J.J. Structural, Ionic, and Electronic Properties of Solid-State Phthalimide-Containing Polymers for All-Organic Batteries J. Am. Chem. Soc. Au 2024, 4, 2300-2311. DOI: 10.1021/jacsau.4c00276)</ref> and with Jeff Hubbel has developed stimuli-responsive polymer-based nanoparticles can encapsulate proteins and RNA but simply warming to room temperature.<ref>(Hossainy, S.; Kang, S.; Emiliano Gómez Medellín, J.; Alpar, A.T.; Refvik, K.C.; Ma, Y.; Vuong, I.; Chang, K.; Wang, T.; Solanki, A.; Rowan, S.J.; Hubbell, J.A. Thermoreversibly Assembled Polymersomes for Highly Efficient Loading, Processing, and Delivery of Protein and siRNA Biologics Nature Bioeng. 2025 DOI: 10.1038/s41551-025-01469-7)</ref>

Rowan's work has been shared on the [http://UChicago%20Pritzker%20School%20of%20Molecular%20Engineering UChicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering https://pme.uchicago.edu] website and elsewhere: "Shape-shifting particles let scientists control how fluids flow",<ref>https://pme.uchicago.edu/news/shape-shifting-particles-let-scientists-control-how-fluids-flow</ref> "Going green with graphite: Researchers turn plant waste into high-tech material",<ref>https://pme.uchicago.edu/news/going-green-graphite-researchers-turn-plant-waste-high-tech-material</ref> and "'Pluripotent' plastic: from one starting polymer, many materials."<ref>https://pme.uchicago.edu/news/pluripotent-plastic-one-starting-polymer-many-materials</ref> In 2024, his work was written about in the [[The New York Times|New York Times]]: [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/02/01/science/shape-shifting-plastic.html "A Shape-Shifting Plastic With a Flexible Future."]

Rowan is a Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS),<ref>(Elected in 2024 https://royalsociety.org/people/stuart-rowan-36799/)</ref> Fellow of the American Chemical Society <ref>(Elected 2018  https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/programs/2018-ACS-Fellows/96/i29)</ref> and Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry (FRSC). Rowan is the founding deputy editor of the journal ''[[ACS Macro Letters]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lodge |first1=Timothy P. |last2=Rowan |first2=Stuart J. |author1-link=Timothy P. Lodge |title=Welcome to ACS Macro Letters |journal=ACS Macro Letters |date=17 January 2012 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=1–2 |doi=10.1021/mz200142m|pmid=35578467 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rowan |first1=Stuart J. |title=Ten Years of ACS Macro Letters |journal=ACS Macro Letters |date=31 August 2021 |volume=10 |issue=9 |pages=1132–1137 |doi=10.1021/acsmacrolett.1c00532|pmid=35549083 |s2cid=239625160 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and succeeded [[Timothy P. Lodge]] as [[editor in chief]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite news | author = ACS News | title=American Chemical Society Names Stuart J. Rowan New Editor-in-Chief of ACS Macro Letters |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/pressroom/newsreleases/2017/december/acs-names-new-eic-of-acs-macro-letters.html |access-date=11 October 2021 |publisher=American Chemical Society |date=5 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rowan |first1=Stuart J. |title=Thanks Tim, from ACS Macro Letters! |journal=ACS Macro Letters |date=16 January 2016 |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=105–106 |doi=10.1021/acsmacrolett.7b01003|pmid=35610929 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
